events.name: dd_event_id
events.description: Primary key. Unique per row, so one per company copy when a contact belongs to several companies. Use for joins and drill-down to a specific copy—not for event counts (use dd_event_activity_id).

events.name: dd_event_activity_id
events.description: Identifies a single event occurrence (e.g. one page view). Shared across a contact's company copies—the same value on every company row for that occurrence, so it is NOT unique per company—and NULL on exposure rows (impressions). Event counts: COUNT(DISTINCT dd_event_activity_id) counts each occurrence once instead of once per company; impressions are excluded automatically, so no tracking-type filter is needed. Count impressions with SUM(quantity); see dd_tracking_type.

events.name: dd_session_id
events.description: Session identifier for this row. Unique per row, so one per company copy. Equals dd_event_id when the session has one event; otherwise the dd_event_id of the first event in the session on this row. Not for session counts (use dd_session_activity_id).

events.name: dd_session_activity_id
events.description: Identifies a single session. Shared across a contact's company copies—the same value on every row in that session, so it is NOT unique per company—and NULL on exposure rows (impressions). Session counts: COUNT(DISTINCT dd_session_activity_id) counts each session once instead of once per company; impressions are excluded automatically, so no tracking-type filter is needed. Often equals dd_event_activity_id when the session has only one event.

events.name: quantity
events.description: Times the event was observed (1 for most events; higher for exposures such as linkedin_ad_impression). With dd_tracking_type = 'exposure', use SUM(quantity) instead of counting distinct ids.

events.name: dd_visitor_id
events.description: Anonymized identifier for a visitor within the Dreamdata system. For identified visitors the dd_visitor_id will be equal to the dd_contact_id. This field is used to calculate the Visitor count as COUNT( DISTINCT dd_pseudo_visitor_id)

events.name: dd_contact_id
events.description: Unique identifier for the contact associated with the event (foreign key referencing dd_contact_id in the contacts schema)

events.name: dd_company_id
events.description: Company for this row (foreign key to companies). When a contact is linked to multiple companies, the same event occurrence appears on one row per company—see table description and dd_event_activity_id.

events.name: dd_tracking_type
events.description: Tracking type of the event. 'activity': standard actions (page views, form submits, etc.). 'exposure': impression-style events such as linkedin_ad_impression. Event and session counts use COUNT(DISTINCT dd_event_activity_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT dd_session_activity_id), which already exclude exposures (their activity ids are NULL)—no filter on this column is needed. For impression totals use SUM(quantity).

events.name: dd_event_session_order
events.description: Order of the event within the session. To obtain the first event of each session use 'WHERE dd_event_session_order = 1'

events.name: dd_is_primary_event
events.description: LEGACY (deprecated for counting): TRUE on the primary-company row when a contact has multiple companies (TRUE when no contact). Older SQL used WHERE dd_is_primary_event before counting dd_event_id; use dd_event_activity_id and dd_session_activity_id instead. Not used for stages, attribution, or influenced-stage analysis.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of the third level i.e. the ad name or keyword text.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the third level within the network.
Most specific level the platform exposes — ad / creative, keyword, etc.

spend.description: Record containing information about the ad hierarchy, with specific network labels and IDs: The IDs are used to match activities and ad, through things like UTM parameters of the activities

spend.name: context

fields.name: campaign
fields.description: Name of the campaign

fields.name: campaign_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the campaign within the network

fields.name: keyword
fields.description: Keyword used in the ad if applicable

fields.name: keyword_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the keyword within the network.

fields.name: match_type
fields.description: Matching type used for the keyword if applicable

fields.name: dd_brand_search_label
fields.description: Branded search label i.e. 'Brand', 'Non-Brand', defined in the Dreamdata platform

fields.name: google_advertising_channel
fields.description: Google advertising channel type from Google's network/campaign classification e.g. 'Search', 'Display', 'Video', 'Demand_Gen'

spend.description: Record containing campaign and keyword parameters of the spend

spend.name: source_system

fields.name: type
fields.description: Type of data source like 'advertisement'.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Name of the data source.

spend.description: Record containing information about the source of the spend data

spend.name: row_checksum
spend.description: Checksum for the row. If any value in the row changes, the checksum changes otherwise it is unchanged. This should only be used to setup incremental table updates.

stages.name: dd_stage_id
stages.description: Unique identifier for each stage entry within the Dreamdata data model. (Primary key)

stages.name: dd_object_id
stages.description: Identifier for the object the stage is built on. This could be the id of the deal or opportunity the stage is built on. The dd_object_id is unique within each stage, but is not globally unique. Relationship with dd_stage_id: dd_stage_id is the combination of stage_name and dd_object_id

stages.name: dd_company_id
stages.description: Unique identifier for the company associated with the stage (foreign key referencing dd_company_id in the company schema). Can be null if no company is associated with the stage.

stages.name: timestamp
stages.description: Timestamp when the stage was reached - not nullable

stages.name: value
stages.description: Value indicating the revenue or similar value associated with reaching the stage.

stages.name: primary_owner

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the owner

fields.name: name
fields.description: Owner's name

fields.name: email
fields.description: Owner's email address.

stages.description: Record containing details about the owner in the source integration

stages.name: journey

fields.name: type
fields.description: Type of the journey. This determines which events are part of the stage journey. The type is set using the Dreamdata Data Hub UI. 'contact level': all activity associated with the contact (see dd_primary_contact_id) of the stage. 'company level': all activity associated with the company (see dd_company_id) of the stage. 'opportunity level': contacts on the opportunity (see object_contacts)

fields.name: start_date
fields.description: Start date of the stage journey. If NULL the journey includes all tracked data e.g. start date is the first tracked data.

fields.name: end_date
fields.description: End date of the stage journey. If this is NULL the stage timestamp is the end date of the stage journey.

stages.description: Record containing details about the journey settings for the stage. The settings are controled from the Dreamdata Data Hub UI.

stages.name: dd_primary_contact_id
stages.description: Unique identifier for a single contact associated with the stage. This is only available for stages built on objects that have a single email associated with it like contacts or leads. (foreign key referencing dd_contact_id in the contacts schema)

stages.name: object_contacts

fields.name: dd_contact_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the contact associated with the stage (foreign key referencing dd_contact_id in the contacts schema)

stages.description: Array containing details about all contacts on the object the stage is built on (can be empty). This is only available for stages built on objects that can have multiple email associated with it, like salesforce opportunities

stages.name: custom_properties
stages.description: Custom stage properties in JSON format. These are selected properties from the object the stage is built on. If the stage is built on opportunities, it will contain properties selected from the opportunity object and if it is built on contacts it will contain properties selected from the contacts object. Which properties are included for each object is controlled through the Dreamdata source UI for the source of the object.

stages.name: source_system

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id for the object record in the source system.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Name of the source system like hubspot, salesforce, etc.

fields.name: object
fields.description: The name of the object in the source system like contacts, leads, deals, opportunities etc.

stages.description: Array containing information about the source systems for the object the stage is built on

stages.name: stage_transitions

fields.name: dd_stage_id
fields.description: Unique identifier for the stage transitioned to

fields.name: dd_object_id
fields.description: Identifier for the object for the stage transitioned to

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of the stage transitioned to

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Time of the stage transitioned to

stages.description: Array containing transitions between this stage and other stages. All stages in the array are reached after the this stage, by the same company or contact (depending on the type of stage). This is used for conversion rate calculations as all connected stages are pre-calculated depending on their specific types and can be accessed simply using the stage_transitions array

stages.name: row_checksum
stages.description: Checksum for the row. If any value in the row changes, the checksum changes otherwise it is unchanged. This should only used to setup incremental table updates.
